title: Free browser football manager that sits between casual games and the Football Manager-level complexity.
author: Xolfyy
selftext:
[https://playfootballheritage.com/](https://playfootballheritage.com/)  
  
**AI workflow:** I used AI throughout development as a coding and development assistant rather than generating the game in one shot. I would design a feature or system first, describe the intended behavior and constraints, then use AI to help implement and iterate on it. I tested the result in the actual game, found problems or behaviors I didn’t like, and went back through further revisions until it worked the way I wanted. I used the same process for debugging, UI work, balancing ideas, localization and refining existing systems. The game grew through a large number of small iterations rather than a single generated build.

I’ve been working on **Football Heritage**, a completely free football management game that runs in your browser. No download, account or paywall.

The idea was to make something between lightweight manager games and simulations that can feel like a second job. There are 33 countries with two divisions each, men’s and women’s football, transfers, youth development, facilities, finances, tactics, domestic and continental competitions, and careers that can start anywhere from 1980 to 2040.

I’ve also tried a few less traditional ideas, like visible win/draw/loss probabilities that react to your tactical choices, detailed career setup options, optional cheats, and two experimental real-time modes called Thunder and Blitz.
